readingInstruction: Read 1 Corinthians 16:1-24. Paul closes with practical matters: the collection, travel plans, coworkers, and greetings. Notice the way he combines practical details with spiritual urgency.
settingTheScene: After the soaring heights of chapter 15, Paul returns to earth. Chapter 16 reminds us that ordinary church life, such as money, schedules, hospitality, and greetings, is part of the work of the gospel. The collection is for the poor believers in Jerusalem, a project that Paul was organizing among the Gentile churches. It was a sign of the unity between Jew and Gentile.
observation: “On the first day of every week, each of you is to put something aside and store it up, as he may prosper” (16:2).
“For a wide door for effective work has opened to me, and there are many adversaries” (16:9).
“Be watchful, stand firm in the faith, act like men, be strong” (16:13).
“Let all that you do be done in love” (16:14).
“They have devoted themselves to the service of the saints” (16:15).
“Aquila and Prisca, together with the church in their house, send you hearty greetings in the Lord” (16:19).
“The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you” (16:23).
interpretation:
Paul begins with the collection for the saints in Jerusalem. He gave the same instructions to the churches of Galatia. “On the first day of every week, each of you is to put something aside and store it up, as he may prosper, so that there will be no collecting when I come.” The pattern: regular, personal, proportionate, and planned. The first day of the week is the day of resurrection and of gathering. Giving belongs with worship. Paul plans to send the gift with approved messengers, ensuring accountability.

His travel plans are flexible and subject to God’s will. He will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost, “for a wide door for effective work has opened to me, and there are many adversaries.” Opportunity and opposition often come together. He asks the Corinthians to receive Timothy without fear, and to send him on in peace. Apollos, who he strongly urged to visit, will come when he has opportunity. Notice that Paul does not control his coworkers; he treats them as partners.

Then a series of short commands, like a sergeant’s orders: “Be watchful, stand firm in the faith, act like men, be strong. Let all that you do be done in love.” This last sentence sums up the whole letter. In a church full of pride, division, and misuse of gifts, love is the controlling principle. Paul commends the household of Stephanas, the first converts in Achaia, who have devoted themselves to the service of the saints. Submit to such people, he says, and to every fellow worker. He is glad of the arrival of Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus, for they refreshed his spirit.

The greetings are warm. The churches of Asia send greetings. “Aquila and Prisca, together with the church in their house, send you hearty greetings in the Lord.” The early church met in homes. “Greet one another with a holy kiss.” Paul takes the pen in his own hand to sign: “If anyone has no love for the Lord, let him be accursed. Our Lord, come!” The Aramaic word is “Maranatha,” a prayer of the early church for the return of Christ. It reveals the hope behind chapter 15. The letter ends with grace and love: “The grace of the Lord Jesus be with you. My love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.” Despite all the rebukes, Paul ends with love for the church.
connection: Acts 11:27-30, Romans 15:25-29, and 2 Corinthians 8 to 9 speak of the collection. Acts 20:7 shows the church gathering on the first day. Acts 18:1-3, 24-28, and 19:1-10 mention Aquila, Priscilla, Apollos, and Ephesus. 1 Thessalonians 5:12-13 asks to respect those who labor. Hebrews 13:17 asks to submit to leaders. 1 Peter 5:14 mentions the kiss of love. Revelation 22:20 is “Come, Lord Jesus.” 2 Corinthians 9:6-8 teaches cheerful giving. Philippians 4:15-19 shows the Philippians’ gift.
application:
Decide on a regular, planned amount to give to your church or to the poor, and give it joyfully.

Thank someone in your church who serves quietly, like the household of Stephanas.

Pray “Our Lord, come!” at the end of the day.
prayerPrompts: Thank God for the saints who give and serve.
Ask him to help you do all in love.
Pray for someone in your church by name.
